question: Should RFC 0018 be accepted with its required/advisory condition model, activation-scoped plugin provider API, and explicit `gateway.readiness` selection as the v1 public contract?
rationale: The proposal is technically detailed and proven, but it creates durable operator configuration and plugin API surface whose ownership, naming, and compatibility promises cannot be selected safely by automated review.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Approve the condition model, activation-scoped providers, opt-in selection, and compatibility guarantees, then advance the RFC lifecycle and implementation review.

options.title: Accept core conditions only
options.body: Keep the canonical evaluator and projections but defer plugin registration and operator-selected criteria to a narrower follow-up RFC.

options.title: Defer the readiness redesign
options.body: Retain the current fixed evaluator until Gateway owners identify a smaller contract or stronger operational need.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the condition model, activation-scoped providers, opt-in selection, and compatibility guarantees, then advance the RFC lifecycle and implementation review.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Gateway semantics, public configuration, plugin API compatibility, and release ownership rather than a narrow documentation edit.
